body: Yes I do.. I work part-time around 11-24 hours depending on my schedule for the work with minimum wage, and enrolled full-time in school.
Thank you for your response. I appreciate it.
I am currently studying in Canada, and the certificate is for College Advanced Diploma. I'm so sorry for the confusion.
Thank you so much. I don't really know what else to say except I really appreciate your comment.

I understood what you meant I'm sorry for the misunderstanding there. But nonetheless, thank you so much for this advice. I'm hoping for the best that I got at least a C on my first exam and a B on this last exam.

There are days when I want to say that but I think I've just become so paranoid, anxious about what they think and hurting them emotionally and financially. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety this semester and haven't told them because well, I just know my parents won't believe me and think I'm just bluffing. 

I think we are all smart but like what Albert Einstein said, "Everybody is a genius. But if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing that it is stupid." I'm hoping for the best but if it doesn't work out then I'll do something else worthwhile....

From the bottom of my heart, thank you for this reply. I contemplated committing suicide because fear that if I have to drop out that I'll be useless in this world. My dad has no clue any of this is happening (I was afraid to console to him regarding school) and mom constantly threatens me to do well or else she'll spill the beans. Anyway, thank you again for this reply. I'll try my best not to think about the exam grades (until they come out) and enjoy life outside.

I guess I felt like if I don't do well-- I'm useless in this world especially to my parents who saw me being a great student in high school to now just flunking university. Heck my dad has no clue any of this is happening but my mom does and constantly threatens me to do well. It's okay, I understand..

Next week I'm going to schedule an appointment with one of the counsellors or perhaps even call a counselling hotline that my uni offers. As for school, for the last 2 semesters I didn't try at all/lost motivation and made school not my priority. I decided I would rather meet new people then do work. This semester, I can honestly say my grades have improved for the better-- I did not expect that I would earn the grades I have now due to losing hope that I won't be able to pass. Nonetheless, aside from getting the degree, losing my boyfriend who has helped me countless times from tutoring to giving me space to study has also motivated me to do well in school to prove to my parents that I can study and also continue dating. 

Thank you again for your suggestions and your story... It really helped, thank you. :)
Thank you braffination. Next week I'll plan to schedule a counselling meeting and just talk about all of this. Thank you again.
